title: Fidelity fallback layers & tool-binding SDK playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook that sketches a lightweight, developer-friendly SDK surface and streaming handshake to support progressive fidelity, explicit tool bindings, and deterministic resume semantics for low-bandwidth or flaky clients. Aim is to give product/SDK/serving teams a reference for implementing layered fallbacks that trade fidelity for latency and cost while preserving developer ergonomics.

Context / problem statement:
- Many customers embed the Hosted API in mobile/edge clients with unstable networks. They need partial results quickly and automatic, safe degradation when heavier tool calls or high-fidelity models are unavailable.
- Current hosted streaming surfaces either block until a full response or emit undifferentiated partial text. Tool calls (search, DB, calculator) are treated as opaque ops and make resume/replay correctness difficult.
- SDK ergonomics are key: teams prefer a few small, predictable primitives over ad-hoc callback+frame parsing.

Design goals (must):
1) Explicit fidelity layers (low/medium/high) advertised per invocation and negotiable between client and server.
2) Tool-binding tokens and commit/abort semantics that allow replay or graceful fallback without duplicating side effects.
3) Streaming frames that are compact and typed so SDKs can surface progressive UI updates (title, summary, action-candidates).
4) Minimal surface area for client devs: 3–5 SDK calls and clear defaults.
5) Telemetry hooks for resolution, fallback decisions, and cost/fidelity tradeoffs.

Non-goals (for this iteration):
- Full formal type-system for arbitrary structured outputs (we'll iterate with schema v1).
- Cross-region multi-model federation — out of scope for initial SDK surfaces.

User stories (examples):
- Mobile messenger: show an immediate short answer (low fidelity) and replace with a richer answer (high fidelity) when available; if a DB tool is down, synthesize a degraded fallback without repeating DB writes.
- Internal agent: call a remote data enrichment tool; if the tool cannot be invoked within 50ms, proceed with a cached best-effort and mark the enrichment as provisional.
- Admin dashboard: present telemetry for fraction of sessions that used low vs high fidelity and how many tool calls were hedged/fallbacked.

High-level protocol sketch (streaming frames):
- Frames are newline-delimited JSON (compact) with a small type field (t). Minimal frame types:
  - {t: "metadata", id: <session>, fidelity_advertised: ["low","med","high"], model: "r-3b"}
  - {t: "delta", content: "...", fidelity: "low"}
  - {t: "tool_call", tool: "search", call_id: "c_42", args: {...}, expected_effects: ["read"], timeout_ms: 1200}
  - {t: "tool_result", call_id: "c_42", status: "ok|failed|timeout", result: {...}, commit_token: "tok_x"}
  - {t: "commit_request", call_id: "c_42", commit_token: "tok_x"}
  - {t: "final", canonical_output: {...}, fidelity: "high"}

Notes on tool_call & commit semantics:
- Tool calls are non-blocking in the stream: the model can emit an initial delta that declares intent to call tool X with call_id. The client SDK should buffer the call and either:
  a) forward to a server-side tool adapter (default) and await tool_result;
  b) if offline, resolve locally with a cached stub and tag result as provisional.
- commit_token is an idempotency/visibility token. A commit_request indicates the model expects the tool's side effect to be durable. SDKs must expose a retryable commit API to the platform. If commit fails, platform should expose a controlled fallback (e.g., revert, compensate, or mark session as inconsistent).

SDK ergonomics (JS + mobile reference):
- Surface: HostedClient.createSession(opts) -> SessionHandle
- SessionHandle.on('delta', (frame) => ...)
- SessionHandle.callTool(toolName, args, {mode: 'auto'|'local-fallback'}) -> Promise({status, commitToken?})
- SessionHandle.commit(callId, commitToken) -> Promise(status)
- Defaults: createSession({fidelity: 'auto', preferredLatencyMs: 150})

Typical flow: createSession -> receive metadata -> receive low-fidelity deltas -> model emits tool_call -> SDK either forwards or local-resolves -> model emits tool_result -> model emits final high-fidelity output -> app optionally calls commit for any requested side-effects.

Structured output & progressive replacement:
- Canonical shape attempt v1: top-level keys: {summary, steps[], actions[], provenance: [{source, confidence}], fidelity_level}. Each delta can patch parts of this canonical object using a simple path-based small-patch format: {t: 'delta', patch: [{op:'set', path:'/summary', val:'short text'}]}
- SDKs should provide a helper to merge patches into a representation and surface stable fields to the UI.

Fallback ladder (policy):
1) Fast-path: low-fidelity model (cheap) -> short summary, no tool calls.
2) Enrichment path: medium fidelity -> speculative tool calls; tool results used if available within time budget. Tool calls marked provisional otherwise.
3) Canonical path: high fidelity model -> wait for blocking tool_result or fallback to a compatible model variant that can approximate the effect without external tool (if configured).

Policy config keys (for product and SDK):
- fidelity_budget_ms: total time budget before switching down a layer.
- tool_timeout_ms[toolName]: per-tool deadline.
- prefer_local_tool_stubs: boolean.
- allow_provisional_side_effects: boolean (default false for hosted dedicated tenants).

Telemetry (events & fields):
- session.start {session_id, fidelity_requested, latency_budget_ms, client_type}
- session.fallback {session_id, from_fidelity, to_fidelity, reason}
- tool.call.sent {call_id, tool, mode(auto|local), dispatched_at}
- tool.result.reconciled {call_id, status, committed: true|false, they_committed_on_server}
- output.finalized {session_id, fidelity, token_cost}
- Note: include sampling flags for verbose sessions to capture frames.

Rollout plan (phased):
- Phase 0 (experiment): internal beta with SDK flag; 5% of internal infra; collect telemetry and bugfix.
- Phase 1 (early customers): expose 'fidelity_ladder' toggle in Console for invited tenants; opt-in only.
- Phase 2 (public): defaults for mobile SDKs; add migration guide on default behaviors.

Operational considerations:
- Cost accounting: count tool-call attempts vs committed side-effects separately. Provide per-token and per-tool billing breakdown.
- Security: commit tokens must be short-lifetime signed tokens. Never allow client to generate a commit token.
- Data governance: provisional/local tool stubs must never leak PII — default off for regulated customers.

Open questions / risks (brainstorm):
- How to represent partial structured outputs so clients can bind UI components without complex merge logic? Lightweight patch is OK, but merging conflicts need rules.
- Who owns local-tool stubs and their lifecycle? Solutions-engineering might produce curated stubs for popular tools.
- UX surface: should SDKs expose provisional flag per field or just per-action?
- Failure modes for commit: do we surface a 'degraded-success' state to end-user or hide it?

Action items / next steps:
- [Elliot] prototype server framing and tiny parser CLI to validate frame shapes (2 weeks).
- [Ravi] implement JS SDK primitives with simple patch-merger; demo in mobile sample app (3 weeks).
- [Product] draft Console toggle + tenant settings (fidelity ladder knobs) and add billing flags (2 weeks).
- Schedule weekly sync with serving-runtime and SDK teams; owner: Sofia.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep frame types minimal; prefer a single small delta shape over many specialized frames.
- Be conservative with default "allow_provisional_side_effects"; enable only via Console toggle for now.

Appendix: example stream (condensed)
metadata
{t:"metadata",id:"s_901",fidelity_advertised:["low","med","high"],model:"r-3b"}
delta
{t:"delta",patch:[{op:"set",path:"/summary",val:"Quick answer: 42"}],fidelity:"low"}
tool_call
{t:"tool_call",tool:"kb_search",call_id:"c1",args:{q:"meaning of life"},expected_effects:["read"],timeout_ms:800}
delta
{t:"delta",patch:[{op:"set",path:"/summary",val:"Short answer: 42 (pre-enrichment)"}],fidelity:"med"}
tool_result
{t:"tool_result",call_id:"c1",status:"ok",result:{top_hit:"Douglas Adams"},commit_token:"tok_c1_v1"}
final
{t:"final",canonical_output:{summary:"Answer: 42 — referenced: Douglas Adams"},fidelity:"high"}

---
This doc is intentionally rough; aim is to converge on a small set of frames, and ship SDK helpers that make the streaming/tool-binding story obvious to developers.
